title: Cliff Richard
wiki_lead:
Sir Cliff Richard (born Harry Rodger Webb; 14 October 1940) is a British singer and actor. He has total sales of over 21.5 million singles in the United Kingdom and, as of 2026, is the third-top-selling artist in UK singles chart history, behind the Beatles and Elvis Presley.
Richard was originally marketed as a rebellious rock and roll singer in the style of Presley and Little Richard. With his backing group, the Shadows, he dominated the British popular music scene in the pre-Beatles period of the late 1950s to early 1960s. His 1958 hit single "Move It" is often described as Britain's first authentic rock and roll song. Further early hits included "Living Doll", "Travellin' Light" and "Please Don't Tease". He had a successful screen career with films including Expresso Bongo (1959), The Young Ones (1961), Summer Holiday (1963) and Wonderful Life (1964), as well as his own television shows on ITV in the 1960s and the BBC in the 1970s. From the mid-1960s, increased focus on his Christian faith and softening of his music led to a more middle-of-the-road image, and he sometimes ventured into contemporary Christian music. He twice represented the United Kingdom in the Eurovision Song Contest, first in 1968 with "Congratulations" and then in 1973 with "Power to All Our Friends".
In a career spanning more than 65 years, Richard has amassed several gold and platinum discs and awards, including two Ivor Novello Awards and three Brit Awards. More than 130 of his singles, albums and EPs have reached the UK Top 20, more than any other artist. Richard has had 67 UK Top 10 singles, the second highest total for an artist (behind Presley). He holds the record, with Presley, as the only act to make the UK singles charts in all of its first six decades (1950s–2000s). He has achieved 14 UK No. 1 singles, and is the only singer to have had a No. 1 single in the UK in each of five consecutive decades. He also had three UK Christmas No. 1 singles; "I Love You" in 1960, "Mistletoe and Wine" in 1988 and "Saviour's Day" in 1990. He was also part of the 1989 Band Aid II version of "Do They Know It's Christmas?", which was that year's Christmas No. 1 single.
By the late 1990s, Richard had sold more than 250 million records worldwide, making him one of the best-selling music artists of all time. He has never achieved the same popularity in the United States despite eight US Top 40 singles, including the million-selling "Devil Woman" and "We Don't Talk Anymore". In Canada, he had a successful period in the early 1960s and again during the late 1970s/early 1980s, with some releases certified gold and platinum. He has remained a popular music, film and television personality at home in the UK as well as Australia, New Zealand, South Africa, Northern Europe and Asia, and retains a following in other countries. When not touring, he divides his time between Barbados and Portugal. In 2019, he relocated to New York.

grok_lead: Sir Cliff Richard OBE (born Harry Rodger Webb; 14 October 1940) is a British singer, musician, and actor who achieved prominence as a pioneer of rock and roll in the United Kingdom during the late 1950s. With his backing group the Shadows, he recorded early hits such as " Move It " and "Living Doll", the latter becoming the first UK number-one single by a British rock and roll act. Over a career spanning more than six decades, Richard has amassed 14 UK number-one singles and seven number-one albums, holding the distinction of the only artist to score a UK top-ten single in each of the first six decades of the chart's existence ( 1950s â 2000s). Richard's clean-cut image, avoidance of the drug and sexual excesses plaguing many rock contemporaries, and public embrace of evangelical Christianity from 1966 onward shaped his persona as a family-friendly entertainer. He starred in films like The Young Ones and Summer Holiday, expanded into adult-oriented pop with later successes including "We Don't Talk Anymore" and Christmas staples like " Mistletoe and Wine ", and received a knighthood in 1995 for contributions to music and charity. Estimated worldwide sales exceed 250 million records, underscoring his commercial longevity. A notable controversy arose in 2014 when South Yorkshire Police raided his home as part of an investigation into an anonymous historical sexual assault allegation from the 1980s, broadcast live by the BBC; no charges were filed after review, with the Crown Prosecution Service deeming insufficient evidence in 2016, and Richard prevailed in a subsequent privacy lawsuit against the broadcaster, receiving substantial damages.
